mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a single month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a single month signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of the instances when HOUST declines for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a single month signals a strong supply-side response, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate robust economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 35% of the instances when RSAFS increases for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a single month, it signals a tight labor market and strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances when UNRATE < 5% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a single month, it signals inflationary pressure and potential monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances when FEDFUNDS > 4% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth is below 2% for two consecutive quarters and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3% in the same period, it signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth < 2% for 2 quarters and UNRATE rises > 0.3%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of the instances when GDPC1 growth is below 2% for two quarters and UNRATE rises by more than 0.3%.
